extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, assignees, patent practitioners, and USPTO/Assignment Division staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and substantive requirements for recording, correcting, indexing, and using assignment/ownership documents (and related notices such as arbitration awards) at the USPTO; plus how an assignee establishes the right to take action in patent matters. Focused on pre- and post-AIA owner/assignee procedural compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government License Rights statement placement
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Government License Rights' statement should appear as the first paragraph of the specification. See 37 CFR 1.77(b)(1)-(3). Providing information concerning government support on a provisional application cover sheet does not satisfy the requirement of 35 U.S.C. 202(c)(6), which requires that a statement be included within the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If invention was made with government support, include the required statement in the specification (not merely on a provisional cover sheet). The statement must be present in any patent issuing thereon specifying government rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing notice of arbitration awards (35 U.S.C. 294 / 37 CFR 1.335)
rubrics_metrics.description: Written notice of any arbitration award under 35 U.S.C. 294 must be filed in the PTO by the patentee (or assignee/licensee). A separate notice is required for each patent involved and must set forth patent number, names of inventor and patent owner, names/addresses of parties, and include a copy of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an award is modified by a court, a notice of that modification (with court order) must also be filed for each patent. Any award is unenforceable until the required notice is filed. Notices should be directed to the Office of the Solicitor, which will process them.

rubrics_metrics.name: What documents are recordable
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments of applications, patents, and registrations, and other documents relating to interests in patent applications and patents will be recorded upon request (35 U.S.C. 261 and 37 CFR 3.11). Typical accepted documents include license agreements and agreements conveying a security interest. Documents constituting transfer/change of title are recordable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents are recorded in the public interest to notify third parties of equitable interests or ownership-relevant matters. Certain documents (e.g., attorney's liens) are not accepted for recording. Refer to 37 CFR Part 3 and MPEP §§ cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation is not determinative of title or validity
rubrics_metrics.description: The recordation of a document is not a determination by the Office of the effect of the document on the chain of title or its validity; the Office will determine effect on title only when necessary (MPEP §§ 324, 325; 37 CFR 3.54).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording preserves history of claimed interests but does not resolve competing claims or legal effect; parties seeking to rely on title should ensure proper documentation and may need later adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when document returned unrecorded (petition option)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document returned unrecorded may, if the sender believes recordation is justified, be submitted to the Office of Petitions with a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 requesting recordation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use petition route only for unusual cases where normal recordation is unjustifiedly denied; otherwise correct and resubmit per instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording date rule (37 CFR 3.51)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of recording of a document is the date the document meeting the requirements for recording is filed in the Office. Documents not complying with identification requirements of § 3.21 will not be recorded; others lacking cover sheet or fee will be returned for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned papers are stamped with the original date of receipt; if corrected and resubmitted within the specified period, the Office will consider the original date of filing to be the recording date. The specified period will not be extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to file required notice (arbitration award enforcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any award by an arbitrator pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 294 shall be unenforceable until any notices required by 37 CFR 1.335(a) or (b) are filed in the PTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required notice is not filed by designated party, any party to the arbitration may file such notice to render award recordable/enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional assignments treated as absolute for Office purposes (37 CFR 3.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments conditional on acts/events (e.g., payment of money) if recorded are regarded as absolute assignments for Office purposes until canceled by written consent of all parties or court decree. The Office does not determine whether conditions have been fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of a conditional assignment for recordation is treated as signifying the condition has occurred; security agreements that do not convey right/title/interest are not conditional assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent purchaser/priority protection (35 U.S.C. 261)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an assignment is not timely recorded at the USPTO, the unrecorded assignment will not be superior to the rights acquired by a third party (bona fide purchaser for valuable consideration) if that third party did not have knowledge of the unrecorded assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely recordation protects against subsequent bona fide purchasers; parties should promptly record assignments to preserve priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment documents should be forwarded to Assignment Division
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment documents submitted for recording should not be placed directly in application or patent files but should be forwarded to the Assignment Division for recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid placing assignment paperwork in application/patent files; proper channeling to Assignment Division ensures recordation and correct indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing/cross-referencing additional patent/application numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for 'indexing' or 'cross-referencing' additional patent/application numbers against a document (other than an assignment already recorded) must comply with 37 CFR 3.11, 3.28, and 3.31; each request must include the document to be recorded and a cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To record a document against additional patents/applications, submit: (A) copy of original document (may be recorded papers showing reel/frame), (B) completed cover sheet (see 37 CFR 3.31 & MPEP § 302.07), and (C) appropriate recording fee (37 CFR 1.21(h) & 3.41). Office will assign a new recording date and update assignment database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment Division handling: formal examination and return process
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents and cover sheets submitted for recording are examined for formal requirements to separate recordable documents from those not recordable. Documents deemed not recordable are returned with explanation. A petition under 37 CFR 1.181 may be filed if sender believes recordation is justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After recording, notification is sent to the correspondence address showing reel/frame number. Assignment Division checks cover sheet completeness but does not compare cover sheet to the assignment document during recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction procedures for unrecorded returned documents (37 CFR 3.51; MPEP § 317.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returned assignment documents/cover sheets are stamped with original receipt date and accompanied by a letter indicating a specified period to correct and resubmit; if corrected and resubmitted within the specified period the original date will be considered the date of recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use certification or Priority Mail Express procedures (37 CFR 1.8 / 1.10) to establish timely resubmission. If not resubmitted within period, corrected papers' receipt date is the recording date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective document requirements for recorded assignment errors (MPEP § 323)
rubrics_metrics.description: An error in a recorded assignment document will be corrected only if a 'corrective document' is submitted that includes: (A) a copy of the original assignment document with corrections made therein, initialed and dated by the party conveying the interest; and (B) a new Recordation Form Cover Sheet (PTO-1595).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify submission as 'corrective document' and indicate reel/frame number where the incorrect document appears. The corrective document will be recorded and assigned a new reel/frame and recording date. Recording fee per patent/application is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of cover sheet errors (37 CFR 3.34; MPEP § 323.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: An error in a recorded cover sheet will be corrected only if (1) the error is apparent when the cover sheet is compared with the recorded document to which it pertains and (2) a corrected cover sheet is filed for recordation accompanied by the recorded document copy and recording fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment Services records cover sheet data exactly as submitted and does not compare cover sheet to assignment during recording. Typographical errors made by the Office will be corrected without charge; other errors require filing corrected papers and paying fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical errors in cover sheet that do not affect title
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original cover sheet contains a typographical error that does not affect title to the application or patent, Assignment Services will correct the Assignment Historical Database and permit the recording party to keep the original date of recordation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit corrected cover sheet, copy of original recorded document, and required fee; include original cover sheet to assist comparison. Check 'Other' and indicate nature of correction on cover sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical errors in cover sheet that affect title
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original cover sheet contains a typographical error that affects title, the recording party will not be entitled to keep the original date of recordation; the date of recordation will be changed to the date the corrected cover sheet is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrected cover sheet must be filed; expect change of recording date and database update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors in recorded assignment documentos (when assignor unavailable)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the recorded assignment document itself contains an error, the responsible party must create and record a new document or make corrections to the original and re-record it. If assignor is not available, the assignee may submit an affidavit or declaration identifying the error and requesting correction, accompanied by a copy of the originally recorded papers, a cover sheet, and required fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit/declaration route is acceptable in absence of assignor; see In re Abacab Intl. Computers Ltd. for precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when assignment/name change improperly filed by another person
rubrics_metrics.description: When owner discovers another party improperly recorded an assignment or name change against the owner's application/patent, the owner must correct the error by filing a corrected cover sheet. If the other party cannot be located or will not file corrective papers, the true owner must record the necessary papers with Assignment Services Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit corrected cover sheet, an affidavit/declaration identifying true owner and reel/frame of erroneous document, required fees, and a summary of the true chain of title to make clear ownership never changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expungement of assignment records is rare and limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to correct/modify/expunge assignment records are rarely granted and will not result in removal of the document image from Assignment Services records. Petitions granted only if (A) normal corrective procedures are inadequate and (B) integrity of assignment records will not be affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if expungement granted for a particular application/patent link, the image remains at the same reel/frame; links to the application/patent are deleted and a redacted version must be recorded. Additional correct assignment may be recorded as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificates of change of name or merger are recordable
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates showing a change of name of a business or a merger of businesses are recordable; a mere change of name is a link in the chain of title and merger documents are proper links in chain of title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record such certificates to establish continuity in chain of title even if legal entity does not change (or does, in case of merger).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title reports and access to title information
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'title report' is a form used by Assignment Division to report owner name of an application/patent as shown in assignment records; title reports may be requested internally (e.g., Reexamination Preprocessing Staff) but may not be ordered by applicants/attorneys. Examiners may obtain title reports via the PALM Intranet. The public can request a certified abstract of title for a fee (37 CFR 1.19(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants/attorneys generally cannot order title reports; use PALM or request certified abstracts per fee schedule if public-certified information needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing ownership to take action (pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To request or take action in a patent matter, an assignee must establish ownership to the satisfaction of the Director by submitting a signed statement identifying the assignee, accompanied by either (i) documentary evidence of a chain of title (e.g., executed assignment) or (ii) a statement specifying where documentary evidence is recorded in assignment records (e.g., reel/frame). For patent matters, documentary evidence must be accompanied by a statement affirming it was or is being submitted for recordation; for trademarks, recording may be required as a condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission establishing ownership must also show the signer is authorized to act on behalf of the assignee either by including a statement of authorization or by being signed by someone with apparent authority (e.g., officer). For assignees of less than entire interest, extent (by percentage) of ownership must be indicated or Office may refuse submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming of record — how an assignee becomes of record
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee becomes of record in a national patent application or reexamination proceeding by filing a statement in compliance with 37 CFR 3.73(b) that is signed by a person authorized to act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the ownership-establishing submission either prior to or at the same time as the paper requesting/taking action; partial assignees must indicate extent of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may conduct prosecution (pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignee(s) who may conduct prosecution are: (1) a single assignee of the entire right, title and interest (may act alone), or (2) partial assignees together or with inventor(s) so that all parties owning any portion of the ownership act together as a composite entity to own the entire right, title and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no assignee of entire interest exists, the combination of all partial assignees and inventors retaining interest is needed to conduct prosecution. If an inventor refuses to join and a petition under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47 is granted, certain assignee actions may be allowed as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Juristic entity representation requirement (effective Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective Sept 16, 2012, an owner or assignee who is a juristic entity must be represented by a patent practitioner for various paper submissions. Juristic entities may sign certain small-entity assertions, disclaimers, submissions under 37 CFR 3.73, powers of attorney, and powers to inspect, but other papers submitted on behalf of a juristic entity on or after that date must be signed by a patent practitioner (see 37 CFR 1.31 et seq.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a juristic entity is represented by a registered patent practitioner where required; certain limited submissions remain allowed without practitioner.
